ref_extractions.title: Vicarious touch: overlapping neural patterns between seeing and feeling touch
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This bioRxiv preprint is the original manuscript for the study that collected dataset ds004563. The abstract explicitly describes the same experiment (EEG with tactile and visual trials, MVPA decoding touch location: little finger vs. thumb), and the Data/Code section references OpenNeuro dataset ds004563. This paper defines a concrete ML classification task.
ref_extractions.epoch_params: tmin/tmax not specified but short stimulus onset markers (event 1=tactile, event 4=visual)
ref_extractions.label_mapping: binary: tactile trials (event 1) vs visual trials (event 4); within-trial decoding of touch location (little finger vs thumb)
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Uses whole-brain EEG data; employs time-resolved multivariate pattern analysis (MVPA) to decode touch location on both tactile and visual trials; tests whether classifier trained on tactile data generalizes to visual data for vicarious touch experiencers.

ref_extractions.title: Vicarious touch: Overlapping neural patterns between seeing and feeling touch
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This is the peer-reviewed version (NeuroImage, 2023) of the same study as the bioRxiv preprint. Same authors, same dataset ds004563, same MVPA methodology for decoding touch location (little finger vs thumb) across tactile and visual conditions. Explicitly uses this specific EEG dataset.
ref_extractions.epoch_params: tmin/tmax not specified in abstract; short stimulus events
ref_extractions.label_mapping: binary: tactile trials vs visual trials; within-condition decoding of touch location (little finger vs thumb)
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Uses time-resolved multivariate pattern analysis on whole-brain EEG data to test whether seen touch evokes overlapping neural representations with first-hand touch experience; classifier trained on tactile trials tested on visual trials.

ref_extractions.title: Embodying an outgroup: the role of racial bias and the effect of multisensory processing in somatosensory remapping
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This 2013 paper investigates Visual Remapping of Touch (VRT) effect and racial bias in somatosensory resonance. It studies tactile detection while viewing faces being touched but does NOT use the OpenNeuro ds004563 dataset, which is a specific 2023 vicarious touch EEG dataset. The experimental paradigm, stimuli, and dataset are entirely different.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Different experiment on different participants; uses Visual Remapping of Touch effect with faces; no reference to the Smit/Moerel dataset.

ref_extractions.title: Socially Intelligent Robots that Understand and Respond to Human Touch
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This PhD dissertation from 2017 focuses on social touch recognition for robotics, creating the CoST corpus of pressure sensor data for gesture classification (pat, stroke, tickle). It has no connection to the OpenNeuro ds004563 EEG dataset or vicarious touch study. The modality (pressure sensors) and domain (human-robot interaction) are completely different.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Uses CoST corpus (pressure sensor data from mannequin arm, 7805 captures), not EEG; focuses on robot pet companion studies; entirely different research domain.

feasibility_reason: The dataset has a clear binary event structure (direct touch vs vicarious/seen touch) with identifiable event IDs (1 and 4), and two relevant reference papers confirm this is a classification/paradigm decoding task using time-resolved MVPA on EEG data to decode touch conditions across 29 subjects.

## Tasks

### Classical Task 1: Touch Condition Decoding (Direct vs Vicarious)
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = -0.2, tmax = 1.5, target_events = [1, 4]
- **Label Route**: `Annotation`
- **Meta Level**: raw
- **Target Definition**:

  | Event | y | Meaning |
  |-------|---|---------|
  | 1 | 0 | Direct tactile touch (feeling touch) |
  | 4 | 1 | Vicarious touch (seeing touch) |

- **Evidence**: DOI: https://doi.org/10.1101/2022.06.21.497107 | DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neuroimage.2023.120269
- **Kernel Notes**: Binary classification between felt and observed touch. Exclude `boundary`, `event_65536` admin markers. Both event 1 and event 4 are short stimulus onset markers (~66,893 trials per condition). Use onset alignment per epoch alignment recommendations. Verify baseline correction parameters given high trial density.

### Normal Task 1: Raw-Meta Condition Extraction
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = -0.5, tmax = 2.0, target_events = [1, 4]
- **Label Route**: `event`
- **Meta Level**: raw
- **Target Definition**:

  | Event | y | Meaning |
  |-------|---|---------|
  | 1 | 0 | Direct tactile touch |
  | 4 | 1 | Vicarious visual touch |

- **Evidence**: Paradigm description and event structure scan
- **Kernel Notes**: Extended window for raw-meta extraction with tmax=2.0s accounting for potential delayed somatosensory responses. Route raw event labels via `event` label route. Exclude boundary markers.

### Potential Task 1: Super-Meta Touch Location Decoding
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5` or `epoch_by_segmentation_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: Needs verification, target_events = see Target Definition
- **Label Route**: `misc`
- **Meta Level**: super
- **Target Definition**:

  | Event | y | Meaning |
  |-------|---|---------|
  | 1 | 0/1 | Touch location (little finger vs thumb) within tactile trials |
  | 4 | 0/1 | Touch location (little finger vs thumb) within visual trials |

- **Evidence**: DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neuroimage.2023.120269 (within-trial decoding of touch location)
- **Kernel Notes**: Super-meta derivation required if dataset provides touch location labels separately from raw events. Document derivation logic, source fields, units, and schema version tags. If MISC labels not present in raw data, derive from paradigm documentation and route to `misc` channel.
